### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c2ac83a230d2eec038502a23a8142153cad814d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `82f6a80c4300e1c4748abb0ab49d04e6ccaeeb61` — the merge of head `8dd02793f0f6b14c9d09098f278993944f350b9b` into base `5c2ac83a230d2eec038502a23a8142153cad814d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 82f6a80c4300e1c4748abb0ab49d04e6ccaeeb61 && git checkout 82f6a80c4300e1c4748abb0ab49d04e6ccaeeb61
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5c2ac83a230d2eec038502a23a8142153cad814d 8dd02793f0f6b14c9d09098f278993944f350b9b && git checkout -B drift-repro 5c2ac83a230d2eec038502a23a8142153cad814d && git merge --no-ff 8dd02793f0f6b14c9d09098f278993944f350b9b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c2ac83a230d2eec038502a23a8142153cad814d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5c2ac83a230d2eec038502a23a8142153cad814d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8dd02793f0f6b14c9d09098f278993944f350b9b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-install-overwrite-readonly.test.ts, .changeset/24030-install-overwrite-readonly-package.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts, docs/adr/0070-package-first-authoring.md, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Inputs: card #24030 (body and all three comments: the triage grade `6223773566`, the claim `6224439457`, the dev report `6225324756`), PR #24055 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at merge-base `b74434c58`), and the check-runs on the head. Not the dispatch order, not the dispatching seat's conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff is one guard call at one door (`packages.ts:1399`–`:1400`), 16 pins, and a changeset. Every accept-set change it implies, read in the cited code:

1. **`POST /api/v1/packages` with `overwrite` (wrapped-body `true` or `?overwrite=true`) over an id `isWritablePackage` judges read-only: `201` with the registry row replaced → `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`, nothing written.** Right. The guard is `requireWritablePackage(deps, qlService, pkgId, …)` (`packages.ts:1399`), the same helper with the same `qlService` engine the four sibling doors pass (`:1591` disable, `:1618` publish, `:2095` revert, `:2290` delete), and that helper is `isWritablePackage` (`packages.ts:527`; `package-writability.ts:85`–`:93`): booted id in `engine.manifests`, or a stored row whose manifest `scope` is `system`/`cloud`. The rule is read, not re-derived, as the card's Done-when orders. The refusal envelope is the sibling doors' own (`422`, `code: WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`, `details.packageId`, the ADR-0070 docs link) — no new error code is minted, as the claim's Clause-② basis states. Pinned on both limbs for all three read-only kinds (code-booted, marketplace-installed, cloud-scoped stored row) plus the query-string spelling, with the row object, its `source`, and the `engine.manifests` entry asserted identical before and after, and the `registry.installPackage` / `protocol.installPackage` / `package.publish` spies asserted uncalled.
2. **The guard sits before both limbs' writes.** Right. It runs before `resolveProtocol` is even called (`:1414`), so the protocol limb's `installPackage` (`protocol.ts:31295`, which itself asks no writability) and the no-protocol fallback `registry.installPackage(manifest, 'authored', settings)` (`:1431`) are both behind it. The `sys_packages` write on the protocol limb (the `package` service's `publish`) is therefore refused too — the dev measured it at base and the pins assert it at head.
3. **Install over an existing id without `overwrite`: `409` unchanged.** Right. The guard is placed after the 409 (`:1378`–`:1383`), so a non-overwrite install keeps the duplicate answer for read-only and authored ids alike. Pinned on both limbs.
4. **Install of a new id, with or without `overwrite`: `201` unchanged.** Right. For an id neither in `engine.manifests` nor the registry, `isWritablePackage` answers writable (`package-writability.ts:92`), so the guard is a pass-through. Pinned on both limbs; the CONTROL rows prove the same spies fire on the allow path, which is what makes the refusal rows' "nothing written" a measurement.
5. **Overwrite of an authored base: `201`, row replaced.** Right. Pinned on both limbs, with the protocol limb's `installPackage` and `publish` call counts.
6. **One accept-set change beyond the card's four rows, disclosed by the dev (deviation 5): the guard is unconditional, not gated on `overwrite`.** The one non-overwrite case it can refuse is an id that `engine.manifests` holds but the registry no longer does — verb `install`, `422`. I read the reach: `engine.manifests` is written only at `engine.ts:4348` (construction) and `:7901` (`registerApp`), never deleted from; `registry.uninstallPackage` (`registry.ts:5679`) removes the row only; and `DELETE /packages/:id` refuses a read-only id at `:2290` before it reaches `protocol.deletePackage`'s `registry.uninstallPackage` (`protocol.ts:27013`). So the state is reachable only by an internal `registry.uninstallPackage` of a booted package, never over the API. In that state the old `201` installed an authored row over a booted id — the exact defect row this card names — so the `422` is the same ADR-0070 D2 rule, correctly applied. **Judged right.** Not pinned, and not named in the changeset's Unchanged clause; that clause is phrased on "a new id", which this id is not, so the clause stays true. Recorded as a note, not a finding.
7. **Public surface.** No export, type, spec schema, or error-vocabulary change; `packages/metadata-protocol`, the predicate, the sibling doors and the ADR-0087 conversion layer are untouched — every hold-off in the claim held. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green: no governed path in the file list.
8. **The pins run where CI sees them.** The new file matches the runtime `local` project's `src/**/*.test.ts` include (`vitest.config.ts:218`) and reaches `packages.ts` by relative import through `../http-dispatcher.js`, so the ablation the dev reports (guard replaced with `null`: the 8 refusal rows red, the 8 CONTROL/409 rows green) measured the committed code. The harness is a real `ObjectQL` (`registerApp` for the booted ids, `registry.installPackage(…, 'authored')` for the scope-only row) and the real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` on the protocol limb.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime` publishes (`18.0.0-next.2`, in the changeset `fixed` group), so a changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong; one is present. The diff narrows a REST door's accept set, so the declaration `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm — it widens nothing and adds no code — and `(narrowing)` is BREAKING (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3). The level `minor` is right: during the launch window a breaking change ships as `minor`, and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses a `major` outside pre-mode. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO mapping, the integrator's one-line fix (install under an owned id, or customise beside per ADR-0131 D6), and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — right, since no spec key, authorable spelling, stored shape or export moves; only a runtime door's answer changes. `Check Changeset` and the Lint lanes that run `check:adr-0087-registration` are green.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on the PR body and in the changeset, matching the claim's line (`6224439457`).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. Dev deviations (report `6225324756`), each answered:

- **`origin/main` not merged before opening.** Answered: the two commits `main` gained since the base touch no file under `packages/runtime`, `packages/metadata-protocol` or `packages/objectql`; the PR reads mergeable; CI ran on the merge ref and is green. Accepted.
- **First full-suite launch used the bare `--` spelling and was stopped before any test ran; the numbers come from the relaunch.** Process hygiene with no bearing on the diff. Accepted.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` not measured locally (exit 3).** Closed by the check-runs: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are green on the head.
- **`test:repo` and the repo-wide eslint not run locally.** Closed by the check-runs: `Test Core` (all six shards and the aggregate) and `Lint · ESLint` are green.
- **Guard placed unconditionally, after the 409.** Judged right in ① item 6; the single extra refusal is the same rule on an API-unreachable state. Note recorded; nothing owed.
- **Base probe printed `served.writable=undefined`.** A probe artefact, not used as evidence. Accepted.

Out-of-scope findings, each escalated:

- **Class (a): an authored install may declare `scope: 'cloud'` or `'system'` and lock itself** (`ManifestSchema.scope` admits it at the install door; `isWritablePackage` then reads the stored row's scope; `DELETE` and `disable` answer `422`; this PR closes the overwrite-to-`project` exit the card's Done-when orders closed). Escalated to the seat for filing as its own card. It is a contract decision at the install declaration, not this PR's surface, and this PR delivers what the card orders for the scope arm. Not blocking.
- **The spec's `overwrite` describe text (`package-api.zod.ts:337`) does not mention the read-only refusal.** Noted for the seat; the sentence stays true (it names the 409 bypass), and a describe-text edit is a `packages/spec` touch owing regenerated artifacts, not owed on this card. Not blocking.

Check-runs on the head, re-read 2026-10-16T22:09Z after the `Test Core` aggregate finished: 40 runs, all completed — 34 `success` (`Build Core`, `Test Core` and its six shards, `TypeScript Type Check` and the four `Type Check ·` lanes, `Lint & Repo Gates` and the eight `Lint ·` lanes, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Auto Label`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `filter`, and the four claim/single-writer/part-of checks) and 6 `skipped` by path filter (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the dogfood shard matrix, `Temporal Conformance`, `Packed-tarball smoke`). None failed, none in progress.

**VERDICT: PASS**
